This study investigates the dynamics of a radio-frequency atmospheric pressure helium plasma jet, specifically focusing on the non-balanced regime where the sheath duration significantly exceeds the gas kinetics time. Utilizing a two-dimensional reduced model, we examine the evolution of the plasma jet, which features a helical structure. The simulation tracks the temporal progression of the propagating filament, which is characterized by a sequence of plasma bubbles. These bubbles are generated by the periodic injection of a helical filament from the electrode, driven by the interaction between the propagating wave and the plasma's non-linear characteristics. The research demonstrates that the filament's propagation velocity is directly proportional to the applied voltage. Furthermore, the study reveals that the bubble length is inversely proportional to the gas flow velocity, while the bubble's width is directly proportional to the applied voltage.

This study investigates the quasinormal modes of string-corrected black holes within the framework of the effective field theory of strings, utilizing the eikonal method. We derive the quasinormal frequencies for scalar, vector, and tensor perturbations, focusing on the high multipole limit. Specifically, we demonstrate that in the high multipole regime, the quasinormal frequencies for vector and tensor perturbations converge to one another, whereas scalar perturbation frequencies remain distinct. We also examine how string corrections influence the shadow of these black holes, observing that while the shadow radius remains independent of the multipole number, its value is sensitive to string corrections. Furthermore, we establish a correspondence between quasinormal frequencies and black hole shadow dimensions, noting that the ratio of the shadow radius to the real part of the eikonal ground state frequency is invariant under string corrections.

Pulsar timing networks (PTNs) offer a powerful means to detect gravitational waves (GWs) by analyzing minute variations in pulse arrival times across multiple PTNs. This approach leverages the PTNs' extensive baseline, which enhances sensitivity to low-frequency GWs. This study introduces a new search strategy that combines traditional cross-correlation techniques with a common-spectrum method. The common-spectrum method utilizes the power spectrum of the timing residuals to identify signals, while cross-correlation directly analyzes the residuals themselves. We demonstrate that the common-spectrum method is particularly effective for detecting low-frequency GWs, whereas cross-correlation excels at searching for high-frequency GWs. By integrating both approaches, the study achieves superior overall sensitivity.

This study introduces a class of generalized Hadamard windows (GHW) that possess support-constrained generator matrices, alongside the derivation of both necessary and sufficient conditions for this support constraint. Specifically, the paper establishes that the proposed support-constrained GHWs constitute an orthogonal matrix set, with specific instances aligning with Welch and Zech products of Hadamard matrices. Furthermore, the study provides explicit expressions for time-domain and frequency-domain characteristics of these GHWs, including the main lobe width, side lobe levels, and the main and null lobe locations. Numerical examples are included to demonstrate the efficacy of the essential and sufficient criteria identified for the support-constrained generator matrix.

This paper introduces a Bayesian approach to identifying influential nodes within networks through sequential experimentation. In this framework, selecting nodes for testing incurs a cost, and the goal is to maximize total node value by gathering data from tests. We propose a Bayesian policy that adaptively determines which nodes to test, using accumulated data to refine posterior estimates of node values. These refined estimates guide subsequent decisions, balancing the trade-off between exploration and exploitation. Our findings demonstrate that this policy achieves near-optimal performance, with a regret bound that converges to the minimax lower bound. Furthermore, we establish that the policy maintains robust performance regardless of the underlying node value distribution.

Unsupervised anomaly detection is a critical challenge in audio processing, particularly when the underlying data distribution shifts. This study investigates the utility of the Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) algorithm for detecting anomalies in audio data. We evaluate UMAP's performance across three scenarios: a baseline with no domain shift, a scenario with mild domain shift, and a severe domain shift. Our findings indicate that UMAP excels at anomaly detection under baseline conditions but struggles when faced with significant distribution shifts.

We introduce a novel ferromagnetic state characterized by sparse, nomadic particles within an SU(N) Fermi gas. This configuration arises from a competition between the tendency of majority particles to form a Fermi liquid and the drive for particles to segregate into distinct SU(N) flavor groups. The resulting ground state exhibits a unique combination of properties: it maintains a zero-momentum center-of-mass wavefunction, displays a Fermi surface composed of isolated islands, and features a spin density with zero mean but finite variance. This system represents a new class of quantum liquids that is both spin- and flavor-segregated, a phenomenon that becomes more pronounced as N increases.

This study investigates the spectral characteristics of 100 gamma-ray pulsars using a stacking method. We employed the Cash statistic to analyze stacked spectra, which revealed that the mean spectrum is dominated by the emission from the majority of the included pulsars. We also examined the dispersion in the mean spectrum to determine the specific contributions of individual pulsars. Our findings indicate that the mean spectrum is well-modeled by a power law with a photon index of $\Gamma = 1.77 \pm 0.02$. Furthermore, the mean pulse profile displays a primary peak at 0.05 ms and a secondary peak at 0.15 ms, which aligns with the average profile. We observed a significant dispersion in the mean spectrum, which is primarily driven by the emission from 10 pulsars. Finally, we identified a distinct group of 15 pulsars characterized by a hard spectrum and a high spin-down luminosity.

This study examines the spectral properties of fractional quantum Hall systems under a magnetic field, specifically focusing on the low-energy excitations of the composite Fermi sea. We demonstrate that the spectral density exhibits numerous peaks, which correspond to the magnetorotons. Furthermore, we find that the sum of the spectral density across all Landau levels remains constant, confirming the spectral sum rule. These findings validate the established characteristics of magnetorotons and indicate that the composite Fermi sea maintains its integrity throughout the entire energy spectrum.

The Intense Energy Events (IEE) experiment, situated on the International Space Station's External Payload Facility, is designed to investigate the characteristics of solar energetic particles (SEPs) and solar X-rays. It comprises four primary components: a hard X-ray detector, a soft X-ray detector, a hard X-ray spectrometer, and a soft X-ray spectrometer. This study presents the performance analysis of the IEE instruments, specifically detailing the response to the most recent major solar energetic particle events.

This paper examines the truncated Boltzmann equation, which incorporates a cutoff on collision velocities to ensure finite cross sections. We demonstrate global existence for small-initial-value solutions across the entire velocity Cauchy plane. This achievement addresses a longstanding open problem originally posed by P. L. Lions.

The presence of errors in labels can significantly degrade the performance of machine learning models, particularly when training data is scarce. This study investigates how various machine learning algorithms respond to noisy labels and compares their accuracy against a baseline. The analysis encompasses both binary and multiclass scenarios, utilizing both balanced and imbalanced datasets. Furthermore, we introduce a novel technique for handling noisy labels in multiclass problems and evaluate its efficacy against other methods.

This study examines the automorphism groups associated with cyclic orbit codes within finite field permutation (FFP) systems. We establish that the group of FFPs functions as a subgroup within the right multiplier group of the underlying field. Furthermore, the paper demonstrates that isometries relative to the Hamming distance constitute a subgroup of the normalizer of a specific subgroup of the right multiplier group.

This study presents the first precise mass determination for a turnoff star in the ancient open cluster M67, achieved through a combined analysis of radial velocity and astrometric data from the Kepler and Gaia missions. The resulting mass, $0.806 \pm 0.006\,M_\odot$, aligns closely with the cluster's age of 3.5–4.0 Gyr, thereby validating the standard stellar evolution models. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that the radial velocity measurements exhibit a sinusoidal variation with a period of 10.3 years and a semi-amplitude of 1.1 m/s, indicating the presence of a companion with a minimum mass of $0.011\,M_\odot$. This object is likely a brown dwarf, which may have been formed via gravitational collapse or captured by the star.

This paper establishes a sufficiency theorem for a framework of eigenfunctions associated with the complex Schrödinger operator defined as $\mathscr{L}_c=-d^2/dx^2+cx^\alpha$, where $c \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. The resulting eigenfunction series provide solutions to the initial-boundary value problem governed by the equation $\mathscr{L}_c u = \lambda u$.

This study introduces a smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) method that integrates a conservative framework with a partition of the unity (PU)-based kernel. The approach employs a density estimation derived from the PU property, utilizing a conservative formulation for momentum and a consistent application of the chain rule for energy. The authors demonstrate that this method is capable of modeling both highly compressible and nearly incompressible fluids. The numerical results indicate that the conservative nature of the scheme effectively prevents unphysical energy drift, while the density-focused strategy ensures superior accuracy in density and pressure calculations. The paper also examines the influence of various parameters on the method's stability and accuracy. The implementation relies on a neighbor search algorithm that identifies the Delaunay triangulation of the particle system. The authors conclude that this method is a promising approach for SPH simulations.

Spectral super-resolution (SSR) is a critical challenge in hyperspectral imaging, aiming to reconstruct high-resolution spectral data from low-resolution inputs. While recent deep learning approaches have demonstrated significant potential in this field, they often overlook the inherent spatial-spectral coupling of hyperspectral data, which hinders the recovery of high-quality spectral information. To address this, we introduce a novel deep learning framework that explicitly models the spatial-spectral coupling. Our method employs a hybrid network architecture combining a pixel-sensitive convolutional neural network (Conv-SSR) with a pixel-wise CNN (Pw-SSR). The Conv-SSR module leverages pixel-sensitivity to capture local spatial-spectral dependencies, while the Pw-SSR module utilizes a multi-branch structure to integrate global contextual information. Experimental results across three public datasets confirm that our proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This study introduces Context Sensitive Object Geotagging (CSOG), a new approach designed to extract objects from images that are spatially localized within the scene. Unlike conventional object geotags, which merely identify object classes, CSOG extends this capability by incorporating contextual details such as the specific location of an object within a city or a structure within a building. We introduce a novel dataset comprising 1,000 images annotated with context-specific object geotags, which are derived from authoritative sources like OpenStreetMap and Google Maps. Our experiments demonstrate that integrating semantic context into object geotags significantly enhances their accuracy and utility.

Accurately estimating dam water storage using optical remote sensing imagery is crucial for flood forecasting, hydrological modeling, and drought monitoring. However, existing deep learning approaches often struggle with generalization when applied to unseen reservoirs due to their reliance on standard Euclidean distance metrics for similarity assessment. To address this, we introduce a novel, end-to-end trainable model that employs a specialized metric learning strategy to enhance the generalization of storage predictions. Our approach integrates two distinct learning strategies: first, a multi-scale feature extraction method that captures reservoir characteristics at various scales, and second, a similarity learning framework designed to refine the prediction of storage values. We validate the model's effectiveness through comprehensive experiments on the publicly available DAMS dataset, demonstrating that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques.

The Quantum Fidelity Saturated (QFS) area serves as a metric for quantifying the quantum information contained within a given state. This article examines the properties of that area, demonstrating that it is invariant under unitary transformations and remains unchanged during the process of pure state purification. Additionally, it is shown that for any specific quantum state, this area corresponds to a function of its von Neumann entropy. Furthermore, an approach to calculate the QFS area for a density matrix is proposed, and its application is illustrated through several examples.

This paper introduces a method for predicting a restaurant's point-of-attraction category using paired text and image data. We propose a new approach that integrates visual and textual features through a mechanism of selective attention. This model effectively captures the complex relationships between modality pairs, surpassing the performance of both the standard CNN-VGG-16 architecture and the standalone LSTM model.

This paper examines the impact of earnings calls on stock price movements by utilizing a novel dataset comprising transcripts from calls between 2004 and 2019, alongside daily returns for 1,000 S&P 500 constituents. We introduce a new methodology for analyzing earnings call transcripts that employs a topic modeling approach to extract key themes, which are subsequently integrated into a machine learning framework designed to forecast post-call volatility. Our findings indicate that the frequency of these identified topics, along with the predicted volatility, significantly correlate with subsequent fluctuations in share prices. Furthermore, we demonstrate that incorporating earnings call data enhances the accuracy of volatility predictions made by models that do not utilize such information.

This study addresses the optimal placement of sensors within both homogeneous and heterogeneous wireless sensor networks (WSNs). In these networks, sensors are distributed across a bounded region and transmit data to a central sink. The primary objective is to determine the minimum number of sensors required to achieve full coverage of the area, ensuring every point is observed by at least one sensor. The analysis considers two distinct scenarios: first, where all sensors share identical sensing capabilities, and second, where sensors are categorized into different classes based on their sensing power. Furthermore, the research incorporates a specific constraint wherein sensors can only transmit data to the sink if their distance does not exceed a defined maximum range. The findings indicate that the optimal sensor arrangement corresponds to the vertices of regular polygons.

We introduce a quantum algorithm designed to filter out specific eigenvalues from a quantum state representing an arbitrary set of eigenvalues. This method employs a polynomial filter optimized via Chebyshev approximation, achieving a time complexity of $O(\log^3 n)$ for filtering an arbitrary state comprising $n$ distinct eigenvalues. When applied to solving quantum linear systems, this filter-based approach surpasses the standard quantum phase estimation method by reducing the required number of qubits by one-half.

We introduce a novel category of compact, stable topological solitons, known as gauged infant skyrmions, within a non-Abelian framework. These structures are defined by a specific compactness condition and arise from the interplay between a non-Abelian field and a U(1) gauge connection. We demonstrate that the stability of gauged infant skyrmions is robust against perturbations, even when the field is compactified. Furthermore, we establish that the existence of these solitons is independent of the specific form of the potential function, provided it is sufficiently smooth and compactified. Finally, we show that the existence of gauged infant skyrmions is generic for a wide range of compactified non-Abelian field configurations.

This study examines the phenomenology of novel physics within the SMEFT framework, specifically targeting the interplay between the Higgs boson and the Higgs portal dark matter (HDM) sector. We analyze the effects of dimension-six operators on the Higgs boson's production and decay rates, alongside the impact of the HDM scalar mediator on the total Higgs width. Utilizing the LHC's Run 2 dataset, we constrain the viable parameter space for the HDM sector. Furthermore, we project the Higgs boson's total width and the associated production of the HDM sector at the future FCC-ee collider. Our findings indicate that the FCC-ee can achieve a sensitivity to the HDM sector that is competitive with that of the High-Luminosity LHC.

Simulating entire biological cells is a formidable challenge that will likely become a defining scientific endeavor of the coming decades. This paper introduces a conceptual framework for whole-cell simulation, outlining a roadmap to transform this vision into a reality. We examine the essential principles and hurdles involved, while also suggesting potential strategies to overcome them.

This study introduces a portable multi-view picture search system designed to retrieve relevant images from a gallery using a single photograph of the target object. The core methodology involves extracting a specific viewpoint's object representation, generating a comprehensive set of object representations from various angles, and identifying the most similar gallery images based on these features. To address the challenge of viewpoint invariance, we propose a novel representation learning framework that integrates a multi-view Siamese network with a multi-view contrastive loss function. This approach generates unified object representations that remain invariant to changes in viewing angle. Experimental evaluations on two multi-view benchmark datasets demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This study introduces a novel hybridization of hyperdimensional computing (HDC) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) designed to enhance the recognition of seizure activities. The approach leverages the high-speed processing capabilities of HDC for feature extraction, followed by the utilization of CNNs for classification. The effectiveness of this hybrid model was evaluated using the UEEPD dataset, which contains EEG recordings from 100 individuals. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 99.99%, surpassing existing state-of-the-art techniques.

We investigate the cosmological implications of the Standard Siren (SS) method, specifically focusing on the Standard Gravitational Wave (GW) Beacon, by analyzing the relationship between the Hubble parameter ($H_0$) and GW sources. Our study examines GW sources from binary black holes (BBH) detected by the Deci-hertz Observatory (DBO) and compares these results with the Hubble parameter derived from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and the SH0ES collaboration. We demonstrate that the GW Standard Siren method can effectively constrain the Hubble parameter, yielding a value of $67.7^{+1.1}_{-1.1}$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ for BBH sources detected by DBO. Furthermore, we find that combining the Hubble parameter from the HST and SH0ES with the DBO-detected GW sources results in a refined estimate of $67.7^{+0.7}_{-0.7}$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, which aligns with the Planck 2018 results. We also analyze the impact of varying the Hubble parameter on the luminosity distance of BBH sources detected by DBO, finding that a 10% variation in $H_0$ leads to a 1.5% variation in luminosity distance. Finally, we explore the potential of future GW sources detected by DBO

The Web Question Answering (Web QA) field has seen significant progress, with numerous datasets released to support research. However, most existing datasets rely on English-only content, which limits their utility for multilingual QA systems. To address this gap, we introduce QALD-10 Plus, a new multilingual dataset comprising 10,000 question-answer pairs derived from DBpedia and Wikidata. This dataset is available in five languages: English, German, Spanish, French, and Italian. We also provide a comprehensive analysis of the dataset's characteristics and evaluation metrics.

Resampling and Relabeling Perceptions (RRP) is a recent paradigm designed to enhance the generalization capabilities of deep reinforcement learning (RL) agents. This approach leverages a hindsight-based reward summarization technique to generate a more comprehensive view of the environment, enabling agents to learn from a broader range of experiences. However, the original RRP framework is constrained by its reliance on a fixed reward function, which restricts its capacity to handle complex scenarios. To address this limitation, we introduce the Executive Ability (EA) algorithm, which integrates a value network to evaluate the significance of individual actions. By incorporating this network, EA can dynamically adjust the weight assigned to each experience, thereby improving the efficiency of the learning process. Empirical results demonstrate that EA significantly outperforms the baseline RRP method, achieving up to a 20% increase in performance across various environments.

Deep learning models for medical image analysis are increasingly utilized in healthcare, yet their deployment risks perpetuating biases present in training data, potentially leading to unfair treatment. This study introduces a new methodology for identifying bias in medical imaging caused by underrepresentation of specific demographic groups. We developed a novel framework to quantify the impact of these biases on model performance, utilizing a combination of adversarial training and data augmentation. Validated across two publicly available datasets—chest X-rays and retinal fundus images—our approach demonstrates the ability to detect bias and effectively mitigate it.

Metric learning aims to train models that calculate distances between data points, with the goal of placing similar instances closer together and dissimilar ones further apart. However, in real-world scenarios, these learning tasks are often hindered by noisy labels, which can severely degrade model performance. To address this, we introduce GAP-Metric, a new approach that combines the stability of proxy-based methods with the discriminative power of anchor-based techniques. Specifically, our method leverages the stability of proxies to filter out noise and uses anchors to enforce strong separation between classes. We further develop a streamlined optimization strategy that maintains the computational efficiency of traditional triplet loss while achieving superior results. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that our approach surpasses current state-of-the-art noise-robust metric learning models.

This study introduces a novel statistical metric designed to quantify the alignment between the density gradient and the correlation structure of galaxy pairs. By applying this metric to the SDSS DR12 dataset, we demonstrate that the alignment angle exhibits a strong dependence on galaxy pair separation, with a clear trend toward smaller angles at tighter separations. Furthermore, we analyze how this angle varies with galaxy properties, revealing that central galaxies in clusters show a stronger correlation with density gradients compared to those in groups, and that galaxies with higher stellar mass and bluer colors display a more pronounced alignment. We also explore the relationship between this angle and the alignment of the spin vector, finding that spiral galaxies at close separations tend to have their spin vectors parallel to the local density gradient, whereas spirals at larger separations and ellipticals at close separations show a weaker or anti-aligned relationship. Finally, we examine the connection between this angle and the alignment of the major axis of the galaxy's two-point correlation function, observing that the two measures are highly correlated.

This study details the fabrication and performance of a novel, high-speed, high-responsivity, and low-noise photodetector utilizing a metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) structure. The device employs a unique MOS configuration featuring a p-type silicon substrate, a silicon dioxide (SiO₂) insulating layer, and a p-type amorphous silicon (a-Si) layer. The photodetector operates in a multiphoton-assisted photo-avalanche mode (MAPD), driven by the avalanche multiplication of holes within the a-Si layer. The avalanche breakdown voltage of the a-Si layer was determined to be 10.5 V. The device exhibits a peak responsivity of 0.55 A/W at a wavelength of 850 nm, with a dark current of 100 nA at a bias of 10 V. The measured noise equivalent power (NEP) is 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁰ W/√Hz, and the bandwidth is 1.1 GHz. The dark current increases linearly with temperature, and the responsivity decreases by 1.1 × 10⁻⁵ A/W per degree Kelvin. This paper examines the connection between localised invariants derived from Macaulay's ideal generators and length functions characterising Cohen-Macaulay rings.

This study utilizes the Nuclear Forward Scattering (NFS) technique to examine the magnetic properties of the four-layered Aurivillius phase, $\text{Bi}_5\text{FeTi}_3\text{O}_{15}$, under elevated pressures. The research reveals that the Fe$^{3+}$ ions within the four-layered $\text{FeO}_6$ octahedra exhibit a magnetic moment of 2.2(1) $\mu_B$ at ambient conditions. Upon compression, the Fe$^{3+}$ magnetic moment increases to 2.3(1) $\mu_B$ at 10 GPa. Additionally, the magnetic relaxation time for Fe$^{3+}$ is measured at 1.2(1) ns at ambient pressure and extends to 1.5(1) ns at 10 GPa. Algorithms are frequently employed to automate trading, yet the associated costs are often disregarded. This study introduces a Bayesian framework designed to evaluate and rank broker trading algorithms by integrating trading expenses. We demonstrate that this approach remains effective even when cost estimates are uncertain, and we validate the methodology using a comprehensive analysis of 1,000 algorithms across 10 financial instruments.

We introduce a new class of add-drop cavities that are optomechanically engineered to achieve full reconfigurability. These devices enable the dynamic, tunable control of both the transmission spectrum and output signal-to-noise ratio. This adaptability arises from the interaction between a mechanical resonator and the cavity's guided modes, which facilitates a Fano resonance. By applying external forces to the mechanical resonator, we can modify the Fano resonance profile, thereby altering the transmission spectrum and the fidelity of the transmitted quantum or classical signals.

Public health interventions are essential for addressing infectious diseases and promoting healthy lifestyles, with their success hinging on the effective communication of core concepts to the public. This study examines the use of Web resources to assess these initiatives, specifically analyzing Web content from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to evaluate its approach to combating antibiotic resistance. We developed a novel methodology to measure the clarity of key messages, the quality of content design, and the accessibility of the Web resources. Our findings reveal that while the CDC's website offers extensive resources, it struggles to effectively convey antibiotic resistance as a critical public health issue.

This paper introduces PILC, a neural network architecture designed for lossless picture compression that is specifically optimized for GPU implementation. PILC employs a straightforward encoder-decoder framework featuring a multi-scale, end-to-end architecture. The design prioritizes practical application by utilizing a compact model size and ensuring high computational efficiency. The resulting compressed bitstream is reconstructed into an image using a dedicated palette decoder. PILC's performance is evaluated against the lossless reference standard BPG and various neural competitors on the KODIM dataset. The results demonstrate that PILC achieves superior compression efficiency compared to all tested methods, surpassing BPG by factors of 1.2x to 2.5x.

This study reports the initial observation of $B^{+} \to D_s^{+}K^{+}K^{-}$ decays, utilizing a data sample of $3.0 \times 10^7$ $B\bar{B}$ pairs collected by the BESIII detector at the BEPCII collider. The branching fraction is determined to be $\mathcal{B}(B^{+} \to D_s^{+}K^{+}K^{-}) = (1.0 \pm 0.8 \pm 0.3) \times 10^{-5}$, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second is systematic. Additionally, the analysis searches for $B^{+} \to D_s^{+}\phi$ decays, finding no evidence for this process. An upper limit on the branching fraction is established at the 90\% confidence level: $\mathcal{B}(B^{+} \to D_s^{+}\phi) < 1.1 \times 10^{-5}$.

This study addresses the problem of transferring mass from a source distribution to a target distribution, with an emphasis on robustness against outliers in the source data. We introduce a novel optimal transfer framework that incorporates an outlier fraction parameter, $\alpha$, to mitigate the impact of outliers. This approach extends the traditional optimal transport formulation by applying a penalty to the transport cost for the top $(1-\alpha)$-quantile of costs. We demonstrate that this proposed method is equivalent to a specific Wasserstein barycenter problem, with the solution derived as the weighted geometric mean of the $(1-\alpha)$-quantile Kantorovich potentials. Furthermore, we establish that the resulting transport cost is Lipschitz continuous with respect to $\alpha$, with a constant that depends solely on the diameter of the support. We also provide a proof of the scheme's outlier resistance, showing that the estimated cost converges to the true optimal cost as $\alpha$ approaches zero. Finally, we evaluate the method's performance through numerical experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

This paper introduces a new method for creating collaborative AI agents capable of learning to work alongside humans through RL. The approach relies on a human choice model that integrates the player's personal traits with in-game conditions to forecast their next move. The agent then selects actions that maximize alignment with this model. We apply this framework to a collaborative card game where the agent's primary goal is to boost the player's enjoyment. Our findings indicate that agents utilizing the human choice model achieve significantly higher alignment scores than those employing alternative strategies, such as attempting to predict the player's specific objectives.

We examine the behavior of heavy superpartners within the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM), specifically focusing on scenarios where the scalar sector mass hierarchy is inverted relative to the fermion hierarchy. In such a setup, the scalar sector is significantly heavier than the fermions, implying that the scalars decouple. We demonstrate that the Standard Model (SM) Higgs boson mass is not constrained by the supersymmetric limit of $m_{h}^{SM} \leq m_{h}^{\mathrm{EFT}}$, where $m_{h}^{\mathrm{EFT}}$ represents the one-loop SM prediction in the decoupling regime. Instead, the Higgs boson mass can be substantially larger, potentially approaching the Planck scale. This phenomenon arises because the supersymmetric limit of the Higgs boson mass is not necessarily the Standard Model limit in the decoupling regime. We also investigate the implications of this result for the Higgs boson width, its total decay rate, and the associated experimental signatures.

The necessity for effective visual communication has driven the widespread adoption of data visualization across numerous fields. Although prior research has examined how data visualization proficiency varies by domain, it has largely overlooked the influence of individual spatial skills and specific task characteristics. This study investigates the relationship between these factors and visualization performance across diverse professional groups. We conducted a comparative analysis involving 120 participants from three distinct disciplines: biology, finance, and engineering. Participants completed a series of tasks designed to assess their ability to interpret 2D and 3D visualizations. Results indicate that performance levels are closely linked to both spatial ability and the specific nature of the tasks, rather than the participant's professional background. Furthermore, we introduce the concept of "professional variations," which refers to distinct patterns in task performance that transcend specific domains. These variations are better explained by a combination of spatial skills and task attributes, suggesting that future visualization design should prioritize these elements over domain-specific assumptions.

This paper introduces Clause Collection Cycles (CCCs), a class of inferences that generalize the established factoring and tiling rules. Like those previous inferences, CCCs are applicable to resolution refutational proofs. However, they offer greater flexibility by not requiring the strict condition that every clause within the inference set be inferred exactly once. Instead, they permit scenarios where one or more clauses are derived multiple times.

Graph neural networks (GNNs) have proven highly effective for node classification, leveraging the aggregation of neighbor features to enhance performance. However, they face significant challenges when applied to graph retrieval tasks, primarily due to the necessity of processing large-scale graphs and the inherent computational complexity involved. This paper introduces a novel retrieval framework that utilizes GNNs to simultaneously extract embeddings for both the query and the target graph. By aligning these embeddings within a shared latent space, the approach facilitates efficient similarity measurement. We evaluate our method on two distinct retrieval scenarios: identifying similar subgraphs within a massive graph and performing graph-to-graph matching. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance across both scenarios.

We present a novel framework for modeling transient dynamics in time series data. This approach leverages techniques from the NLP domain, including BERT and GPT, to create models that are both context-aware and autoregressive. By utilizing these methods, we achieve a context-aware modeling of transient dynamics in time series data. This paper examines the allocation of divisible resources, such as electricity, among multiple users with varying demands. We introduce a straightforward, fair method for distributing these resources that functions as a division algorithm. Our approach is grounded in a specific variant of the $m$-ary division algorithm proposed by J. W. S. Cassels in 1957. We demonstrate that this algorithm satisfies fairness criteria including proportionality, envy-freeness, and surplus freedom. Additionally, we establish that the algorithm is strategy-proof, meaning users cannot gain a better outcome by misrepresenting their preferences.

Event coreference resolution involves grouping text segments that refer to the same occurrence. This research introduces a newly developed dataset named CCPE-CC, which contains 100 news articles detailing ten contentious political events. The collection includes annotations for event mentions, arguments, and event coreferences. Additionally, the study presents a novel graph-based method for identifying event coreferences, which incorporates textual features, document-level context, and inter-document temporal relationships. Preliminary findings indicate that leveraging context from multiple documents substantially enhances coreference identification accuracy.

This study examines the complementarity knapsack problem (CKP), a recent variant of the knapsack problem where specific pairs of variables are constrained to have at least one non-zero value. We introduce novel concepts of facets and derive multiple facet-generating substructures for the feasible region of CKP. Furthermore, we establish new categories of facets for CKP that differ from previously documented structures in the literature.

This paper introduces the notions of generalized $(m,n)$-derivations and generalized $(m,n)$-centralizers within semiprime algebras, examining their interconnections and relationships. Furthermore, we demonstrate that such structures reduce to standard centralizers and derivations under specific conditions.

We demonstrate that applying the spin constraint to the spin part of Weinberg's two-factor exponential naturally generates the spin-dependent terms found in the non-relativistic reduction of the Dirac equation for hydrogen. By employing the spin spherical harmonics method, we derive a spin constraint equation that parallels the spin part of Weinberg's formulation. This parallelism allows for the construction of a spin-dependent potential suitable for a non-relativistic Hamiltonian, which successfully reproduces the ground state energies of hydrogen atoms in ordinary, positronium-like systems, and muonic atoms.

We define transversal groups for nonlinear projections within $\mathbb{R}^n$ and utilize them to establish new Faverd-like theorems concerning the dimensions of one-dimensional projection images and their orbits. These results extend upon the foundational work of Bourgain and Guth.

This paper introduces a directed search framework for reinforcement learning that facilitates goal-directed behavior within uncertain environments. The method employs a directed policy $\pi_{dir}$ to guide a policy learning algorithm, $\pi_{learn}$, toward specific objectives. We propose a novel, model-based directed control approach, termed Tube MPC, which leverages a local model of the system dynamics to generate robust trajectories. By accounting for bounded model uncertainty and external disturbances, Tube MPC ensures that the resulting policy $\pi_{tube}$ maintains robustness against perturbations. Theoretical analysis confirms that $\pi_{tute}$ can steer the learning algorithm to a Nash equilibrium. Furthermore, we demonstrate the efficacy of Tube MPC by applying it to a robotic arm task involving object manipulation under uncertainty. Experimental results indicate that directing $\pi_{tute}$ via a directed policy significantly enhances the efficiency of the learning process compared to standard imitation learning approaches.

We introduce a generalized semiclassical framework for analyzing the Hall effect in noncentrosymmetric systems, which incorporates the third-order Berry curvature alongside the Berry curvature itself. This approach demonstrates that the Berry curvature's third-order component generates an additional unusual Hall contribution, matching results derived from the full quantum formalism. Furthermore, we show that the magnitude of this intrinsic unusual Hall effect is determined by the system's Fermi surface geometry.

We introduce a method for creating scalable, data-driven representations of software call graphs that remain resilient to minor modifications. This approach constructs a collection of call graphs from a set of programs, treating each as a node in a graph where edges denote the presence of shared functions. To capture the structural nuances of this graph, we apply a multi-step process: first, we use a community detection algorithm to group nodes into clusters; second, we employ a graph embedding technique to convert these clusters into vectors. To further enhance interpretability, we utilize a clustering method to identify and group similar vector representations. These steps yield a highly scalable system that is both interpretable and effective at distinguishing between semantically related programs.

The One Billion Word Benchmark (OWB) has been widely adopted to assess the quality of language models, yet it is often treated as a standalone metric. This study examines the OWB's underlying assumptions and their impact on model evaluation, specifically focusing on the assumption that information value correlates with its predictive utility. We demonstrate that this premise is flawed by showing that information gain can favor models which generate unhelpful or spurious correlations. Our findings indicate that the OWB's effectiveness as an evaluation metric is compromised, suggesting that researchers should prioritize alternative metrics that possess more robust theoretical foundations.

We report on the first direct observation of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) within a flare current sheet, utilizing the Nobeyama Radio Polarimeter (NRP) at 17 GHz. This flare, occurring on 2017 August 21, was a large-scale event that produced a Type III radio burst and a Type II radio burst. Our analysis reveals that the 17 GHz emission from the flare's current sheet exhibits QPOs with a period of approximately 10 seconds. These oscillations are localized to a region spanning 100,000 to 200,000 kilometers in the flare's lower atmosphere. We propose that the QPOs originate from the periodic expansion of the flare's current sheet, a phenomenon driven by the repetitive ejection of magnetic flux ropes.

Anomaly detection is a critical component of industrial quality inspection, where the goal is to identify deviations from normal patterns. This paper introduces a novel multi-scale detection method that leverages a one-dimensional wavelet decomposition to extract features across various scales. The approach utilizes the Contrario framework to identify anomalies based on these multi-scale features. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques, achieving a 10% improvement in the Area Under the Curve (AUC) metric.

This paper investigates the dispersion-generalized Kadomtsev-Petviashvili I (KP-I) equation, defined as $\partial_t u + \partial_x^3 u + \partial_x^2 u + u_{yy} + u^2 = 0$ (with a specific sign convention for the nonlinear term, though the original text uses $u^2$), where the nonlinear term is modified by a dispersion coefficient $\alpha$: $\partial_t u + \alpha \partial_x^3 u + \partial_x^2 u + u_{yy} + u^2 = 0$. The study focuses on establishing low irregularity well-posedness for this dispersion-generalized equation.

This study examines the stability of Kramers' degeneracy within open quantum systems featuring a single parity-time (PT) symmetry-breaking exceptional point. We demonstrate that degeneracy can be disrupted by coupling to the environment, provided the spectral characteristics of the reservoir's density of states align with specific criteria. Furthermore, we derive the necessary conditions for restoring parity and time-reversal symmetry in such open systems.

This study introduces a new approach for forecasting future Channel State Information (CSI) responses in rapidly moving, high-density massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (m-MIMO) networks. By leveraging the inherent sparsity of CSI in the angular domain, our method utilizes a low-rank decomposition technique to estimate sparse solutions. We further develop a proximal gradient algorithm to solve the resulting convex optimization problem. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that this proposed algorithm delivers highly accurate CSI predictions, significantly outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods.

The objective involves determining the probability that a pixel in a disparity map falls below a specified threshold. We introduce a novel estimation approach grounded in a mixture of Beta distributions, which utilizes the method of moments to derive its parameters. This paper examines the pointwise behavior of the Szeg\H{o} kernel on the boundary of a complexified Riemann domain, specifically addressing the case of a compact base manifold. We establish a generalization of the standard Szeg\H{o} kernel asymptotics, which holds true under the assumption that the boundary is strictly pseudoconvex. This result extends previous findings by H. Seshadri regarding Grauert tubes on the boundary. Additionally, we provide an explicit formula for the leading coefficient in the asymptotic expansion, which is determined by the curvature of the underlying metric.

This study introduces a novel algorithm for reconstructing matrices from their line charts. By utilizing a greedy strategy, the approach determines the optimal ordering of rows based on maximizing the sum of absolute differences between adjacent elements. This methodology is compared against a previously published technique by Roussopoulosus, which relies on a dynamic programming approach. The effectiveness of both strategies is evaluated through a series of numerical experiments.
We have demonstrated that the conjecture proposed by M. A. Lee regarding the topology of irreducible modules is accurate.

The Java ecosystem has grown significantly in size and complexity, with developers relying on third-party libraries to address this challenge. This paper examines the stability of Java dependencies by analyzing 1,000 popular packages from Maven Central, tracking their source code through 1.5 million commits across 1,000 repositories. We identify that 70% of these packages contain at least one unstable dependency, with an average of 1.5 failures per package. Our analysis reveals that 70% of these failures originate from the foundational Java language itself rather than other libraries. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the incidence of failures in specific packages remains consistent regardless of the underlying Java version, indicating that the Java community struggles to maintain backward compatibility.

We examine the entanglement properties of two independent, biphoton-regulated, non-classical chains, demonstrating that a specific, tunable interaction between them arises from their kinship and rivalry. This phenomenon is characterized by the generation of two-photon entanglement between the chains, a process that can be regulated by adjusting the initial state of the biphotons that mediate the interaction.

This study examines multistage distributionally resilient optimization (DRSO) problems where distributional assumptions rely on probability measures drawn from a known reference distribution. We introduce a novel scenario-based framework that integrates distributional robustness, enabling the optimization of distributions across various stages. Our approach leverages the Total Variation (TV) distance to define ambiguity sets, which we demonstrate are both convex and computationally efficient to solve. Furthermore, we establish that this framework is robust against the curse of dimensionality regarding the number of stages, and we provide empirical evidence supporting its practical efficiency.

This paper introduces a new recurrent neural network (RNN) framework designed for action prediction, which employs a radial basis function (RBF) kernelized feature mapping layer to transform input features into a higher-dimensional space. This approach allows the model to effectively capture non-linear relationships within the data. We evaluated the method using two datasets: a 3D human pose dataset and a 3D human motion dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed architecture outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

We introduce a new deep thermalization framework that utilizes a sequence of unitary gates to map an arbitrary initial state to a thermal state. This approach is solvable, meaning the optimal circuit depth and the specific circuit parameters can be analytically determined. We demonstrate that this framework is robust against circuit depth errors and that the resulting thermalization process is resilient to perturbations in the initial Hamiltonian. Furthermore, we show that this method is scalable, allowing for the study of infinite systems in the thermodynamic limit.

This study establishes the boundedness criteria for a class of symbol-based pseudo-differential operators defined on uniform trees, alongside investigating the conditions under which they become nuclear. As a consequence, several applications are derived regarding specific bounded subsets within these symbol spaces.

The proliferation of smartphones has driven the creation of specialized network architectures designed to prioritize their unique traffic patterns. This paper introduces a novel approach to analyzing smartphone traffic within emerging 5G mobile networks. By examining the dominance of smartphone visibility, we evaluate how the characteristics of smartphone data streams differ from those of other devices. Our findings indicate that smartphone visibility is the primary factor shaping the architecture of next-generation networks.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved remarkable success in various domains, including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition. However, these models often exhibit overconfidence when encountering out-of-distribution (OOD) data, a trait that poses significant risks in critical sectors like autonomous driving and medical diagnostics. To address this, we introduce the Chamfer Out-of-Distribution Sample Challenge (CODE), which evaluates the ability of OOD detection methods to identify anomalies. This challenge comprises a dataset of 100,000 in-distribution images and 100,000 out-ofdistribution images. The dataset includes a validation split of 20,000 in-distribution and 10,000 out-ofdistribution samples, along with a test set containing 80,000 in-distribution and 100,000 out-ofdistribution samples. We have also released a baseline OOD detection method to facilitate the evaluation of competing approaches. The competition results demonstrate that the proposed baseline successfully identifies OOD samples, establishing a benchmark for future research.

This study presents the first azimuthal angle distributions for 2-jet, 3-jet, and 4-jet events in proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, utilizing data from the CMS detector at the LHC. The analysis focuses on jets with transverse momenta exceeding 30 GeV and rapidities within the pseudo-rapidity range |y| < 2.4. The measured distributions are compared against predictions from the Parton Shower Monte Carlo (PYTHIA 8) and the Parton Branching (HERWIG 7) event generators, alongside next-to-leading order (NLO) calculations from the Parton Shower Monte Carlo (POWHEG) framework. Additionally, the study evaluates the sensitivity of these distributions to the strong coupling constant, $\alpha_s$, by comparing data against theoretical predictions.

The rapid advancement of deep learning has significantly accelerated research in computer vision, leading to the development of numerous powerful algorithms. In the context of education, these visual learning techniques have been applied to diverse fields, including medical imaging, industrial inspection, and autonomous driving. However, the majority of existing deep learning approaches depend heavily on large volumes of manually annotated data, which is often time-consuming and expensive to create. To address this challenge, this survey examines recent deep learning methodologies that function without manual annotations, specifically focusing on semi-supervised and unsupervised learning. The paper begins by providing a brief overview of the current state of the art in visual education, followed by a detailed analysis of recent progress in non-supervised learning techniques. Finally, the work concludes with a discussion of the limitations of current methods and outlines potential future research directions in this domain.

Outlier detection is a vital task in data analysis, yet the majority of existing methods are designed for tabular data, leaving point cloud data largely unaddressed. This paper introduces RECol, a reconstruction-based approach that identifies anomalies by leveraging the reconstruction error derived from a learned manifold. By training a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) to map point cloud data to a latent space, we can detect outliers based on the error associated with this reconstruction. We evaluate RECol against various state-of-the-art techniques using benchmark datasets, including ShapeNet, ModelNet, and ModelNet40. Our results demonstrate that RECol achieves performance comparable to current leading methods.

This study examines the uniform behavior of solutions within a specific category of non-linear Young equations. We establish that for these equations, the limit exists uniformly for the domain, which implies uniqueness of solutions in distribution. Furthermore, the research derives distributional criteria for these non-linear Young equations, which are defined by the standard form where dX_t = X_t^2 dt + dB_t, with the domain being the set of real numbers excluding zero and the process starting at zero. We present an improved calculation of the neutrino polarizability, utilizing the latest chiral perturbation theory (ChPT) results for the axial form factor of the nucleon. Our findings indicate that the precision of the current polarizability estimate exceeds the theoretical uncertainty of the input axial form factor data.

This study examines the oscillatory behavior of the mean field model describing interactions between neurons and glial cells. We demonstrate that under specific conditions, the model exhibits a stable limit cycle, representing a dynamic equilibrium between neuronal and glial populations. Furthermore, we identify parameter regimes where the model displays a stable steady state coexisting with a stable limit cycle, a scenario indicative of bistability.

This study examines the quantum behavior of a neutral spin-1/2 particle within a spatially varying magnetic field. We identify a specific field configuration that induces a non-trivial topological structure, enabling the system to function as an effective Abelian anyon. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the system can operate as a non-Abelian anyon, a realization that appears feasible in laboratory settings. Finally, we explore the topological phase's potential applications in quantum computation and anyon-based quantum memory.

We introduce a novel method for boundary erosion in complex domains, which operates by shrinking the boundary based on the initial values of a function defined throughout the entire region. Unlike traditional techniques that shrink regions according to boundary values alone, this function's definition across the whole domain dictates the erosion pattern. The process is initiated by the first hitting time of a particle reaching the boundary, with the erosion magnitude determined by this stochastic parameter. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the resulting erosion is a monotonically decreasing function of the initial values, and we provide explicit formulas for the expected erosion in one-dimensional settings. Furthermore, the method's utility is highlighted through its application to a range of problems, including the identification of outliers, the removal of noise, and the detection of anomalies.

We introduce a hyperbolic family of L-space links, $\{K_n\}_{n\geq 2}$, and establish bounds for their hyperbolic volume. For every such link $K_n$, we define a formal semigroup $\mathcal{S}_n$ and demonstrate that the set of normal surfaces within $S_n$ corresponds exactly to those of the lower states of the link state graph. Furthermore, we prove that this state graph is isomorphic to the link's dual triangulation's state graph. Leveraging these findings, we derive formulas calculating both the number and volumes of distinct states.

This study examines the Boltzmann equation governing a gas of particles subject to random, time-varying potential. We demonstrate that the Boltzmann equation admits a formal asymptotic limit as the Knudsen number approaches zero, yielding a Vlasov-type equation that accounts for both the Knudsen diffusion of particles and binary collisions. Subsequently, we show that under the ansatz of local equilibrium, this asymptotic Vlasov equation can be reduced to a set of Euler-like partial differential equations featuring non-constant diffusion coefficients.

This study introduces a novel benchmark dataset for endoscopic video analysis, comprising 1,000 frames annotated with surgical instruments, endoscope, and tissue regions. This collection is designed to evaluate the efficacy of deep learning-based object detectors in identifying surgical tools within such footage. To address the scarcity of data, we apply data augmentation techniques to expand the training set. Furthermore, we assess the performance of detectors from the YOLO and Faster R-CNN families on the benchmark. Our findings indicate that the YOLOv4 model achieves the highest mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.81, surpassing the previously reported YOLOv3 result of 0.69.

Identifiers serve as a fundamental component of source code, functioning as the primary mechanism for naming variables, functions, classes, and other elements. While prior research has extensively examined identifier naming conventions, it has largely overlooked the analysis of suffixes that denote types and roles. This study addresses this gap by investigating the creation, organization, and meaning of these identifier suffixes. We conducted a comprehensive analysis of how suffixes are formed, their structural patterns, and their specific roles across various programming languages. Furthermore, we explored the relationship between syntax patterns and broader semantic contexts, such as naming conventions and design principles. Our findings reveal that suffix usage is not arbitrary; rather, they are deeply connected to language design, software engineering practices, and type systems.

We establish a $\square_q$-algebra framework for the Fock space associated with the vertex operator algebra corresponding to affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ at level one. This construction relies on a $\square_q$-module architecture developed within the $q$-shuﬄe algebra. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this framework yields a $\square_q$-module structure on the Fock space of the fermionic vertex operator algebra at rank one.

This study introduces a novel data-driven approach to examine grain growth in duplex and triplex microstructures. The method utilizes a data-informed weighting scheme to assess the impact of individual grain populations on growth kinetics, thereby revealing the dominant mechanisms controlling these processes. By analyzing a dataset of grain growth trajectories from triplex systems, the research demonstrates that grains within a duplex subsystem can exhibit either faster or slower growth rates compared to those in the third, distinct population. Furthermore, the findings indicate that grain growth kinetics in triplex alloys cannot be adequately described by a single power law; instead, they are better represented by a weighted sum of three distinct power laws, with each corresponding to one of the three grain populations.

This paper introduces a novel framework for assessing 3D human pose and shape estimation, a field that has seen significant advancements in recent years. While prior research has primarily focused on improving model accuracy, this work aims to enhance the field by establishing a comprehensive evaluation framework that examines the interplay between input data quality, algorithmic performance, and real-world applications. We begin by defining a taxonomy of evaluation metrics and categorizing them based on their utility. Subsequently, we analyze the relationship between input data quality and algorithmic performance, demonstrating that current pose and shape estimation models perform optimally in controlled environments with high-quality inputs. Finally, we investigate the practical utility of these algorithms by evaluating their effectiveness in downstream tasks, such as human-object interaction prediction.

We investigate the superconducting properties of a two-dimensional lattice of weakly interacting quantum dots, where tunneling between dots is mediated by Cooper pairs. The system incorporates strong on-site Coulomb repulsion and a finite density of states near the Fermi level. Our analysis reveals that even at low concentrations of dots, the system exhibits a superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$) that increases exponentially as the dot density approaches zero. Furthermore, we demonstrate that within this framework, the superconducting state can manifest as either a BCS-like or a Bose-Einstein condensate of Cooper pairs.

This paper introduces a classification theory for machine learning, establishing a rigorous mathematical framework to address the inherent complexity of the field. Our approach defines machine learning as a problem of minimizing the expected loss of a predictor, where the predictor is selected by optimizing a specific objective function. We demonstrate that, under certain conditions, this objective function can be expressed as a sum of the expected loss and a complexity term. This complexity term is determined by the mutual information between the predictor and the training data. Furthermore, we prove that minimizing this objective is equivalent to minimizing the expected loss alongside a regularization term derived from a specific divergence measure. Finally, we apply these theoretical findings to several machine learning scenarios, including supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning.

This paper introduces a novel ideal terminal sliding-mode control (ITSMC) algorithm designed for second-order dynamic systems. By employing a newly defined ideal sliding surface, the proposed ITSMC framework ensures that system states reach the surface in a finite time, subsequently driving them to the equilibrium point in a bounded duration. Distinct from conventional terminal sliding-mode control (TSMC), which typically suffers from the chattering phenomenon, this approach eliminates such issues entirely. Furthermore, the analysis demonstrates that the convergence speed within the ITSMC scheme is adjustable by the controller designer. To substantiate these claims, numerical simulations are provided for comparison against traditional TSRC methods.

Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are essential for modern society, yet their internal architecture remains largely unknown. This study introduces a non-destructive, quantitative method to characterize the stratified internal structure of LIBs by analyzing their response to ultrasonic vibrations. By applying a low-frequency ultrasonic signal to the battery's exterior and measuring the resulting electrical current, we detect mechanical vibrations within the cell. Utilizing a theoretical model that correlates the battery's internal layered architecture with its ultrasonic response, we successfully reconstructed the internal structure from the measured data. This reconstruction technique is robust enough to handle various stratified configurations and remains effective even when the signal-to-noise ratio is low. Consequently, our findings offer a promising pathway for characterizing the internal structure of LIBs and other layered materials through ultrasonic analysis.

This paper introduces a discrete-time flatness-based control approach for gantry cranes, derived from continuous-time formulations. The method utilizes the first integrals of motion to establish a parametric, closed-form expression for the control input, ensuring exact trajectory tracking. Consequently, the stability of this control law is verified through a discrete Lyapunov function. Furthermore, the proposed strategy is validated via numerical simulations, with results compared against a traditional cascaded PD controller.

This paper addresses the challenge of generating image descriptions under conditions of noisy data. We introduce a cooperative distillation framework that leverages the complementary strengths of noisy and clean datasets. By employing a shared encoder paired with distinct decoders, our approach facilitates the transfer of knowledge from the clean to the noisy data. Experimental results demonstrate that this method surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques in mitigating the adverse effects of noisy data.

We introduce the concept of an arranged Ehresmann semigroup and present a constructive method for its representation within regular ordered semigroups. Furthermore, we develop a functor that maps these arranged semigroups to categories, demonstrating that the image consists of group-categories.

Self-attention mechanisms have become a cornerstone of modern natural language processing, with their efficacy heavily influenced by model architecture. This study investigates how self-attention performance scales with varying dimensions of model width and layers (depth). We demonstrate that while increasing model depth is effective for expanding the vocabulary size, model width offers superior improvements in linear scaling behavior. Furthermore, we identify that the depth-to-width ratio is a critical factor in determining the overall effectiveness of self-attention mechanisms.

This study details the synthesis of BiFeO$_3$ nanoparticles using a sol-gel auto-combustion technique at a low temperature of 500°C. The resulting nanomaterials were characterized via XRD, SEM, TEM, and UV-Vis spectroscopy, revealing a mixed phase of hexagonal Bi$_2$O$_3$ and rhombohedral BFO. Notably, the hexagonal Bi$_2$O$_3$ content was found to be highly dependent on the initial Bi/Fe ratio. The material's photocatalytic efficiency was evaluated through the degradation of Rhodamine B and the generation of H$_2$ gas under visible light irradiation. The findings indicate that the composite exhibits superior photocatalytic performance compared to pure BFO, with the hexagonal Bi$_2$O$_3$ component playing a critical role in enhancing this activity.
